 J U D G M E N T
This is a claim petition filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .15,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by him in the accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 21.07.2022 at about 07.00 p.m., when the petitioner was going in his Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-HY-0999 at opposite Trumpti Wine Store,
Pipeline Road, Yeshwanthapura, Bengaluru, a Car bearing Regn.No.KA-13-C-6770 driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, suddenly stopped his vehicle and opened the right side door of the car.
Due to the said act of driver of the car, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Thereafter, petitioner was shifted to Lakshmi Clinic and thereafter, shifted to Hosmat Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent a sum of .5,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and he was doing Agriculture cum Milk Vending and earning .25,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of car by its driver.
The respondents, being the R.C. owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. In spite of service of notice, 1st respondent did not appear before the tribunal and hence, he has been placed ex-parte.
The respondent No.2 appeared before the tribunal through the counsel and filed the written statement.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.2 denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondent No.2 also denied age, occupation and income of petitioner as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further respondent No.2 contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.

Further contended that at the time of alleged accident, the rider of motor cycle even though the brake system was in order as per IMV report, without a driving license, without competence to ride the said motor cycle rode the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and hit the insured vehicle car and caused this accident.
Further considering the damages stated in IMV Report, it is clearly substantiated that there is gross negligence on the part of rider of motor cycle.
Further contended that the charge sheeted driver/insured vehicle car is primarily liable to pay the compensation for the alleged tort feasor act done by him.
Further the car was insured with this respondent under the policy No.12747575 which is valid from 04.11.2021 to 03.11.2022 and the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prays to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office framed the following:

sentences.text:
Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 21.07.2022 at about 07.00 p.m., at Pipeline Road, Yeshwanthapura,
Opposite Trumpti Wine Store, Bengaluru, when he was riding a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-HY- 0999, due to the rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.KA-13-C- 6770 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition? If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3. What order or award?

6. In order to prove case of petitioner, petitioner examined himself as PW.1, got examined Dr.Krishan Prasad, working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Hosmat Hospital as PW.2 got marked documents at Ex.P1 to 21 and closed their side of evidence.
The respondents did not adduce their evidence either oral or documentary.

7. Heard the arguments on both the sides and perused the materials available on record.
8.

Findings of this tribunal on the above issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative;
 Issue No.3 : As per final order for  the following:-
 -:REASONS:-
9. Issue No.1:- The petitioner contended that on 21.07.2022 at about 07.00 p.m., accident occurred at Pipeline Road, Yeshwanthapura, Opposite Trumpti Wine Store, Bengaluru, when he was riding Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-HY-0999, due to the rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.KA-13- C-6770 by its driver in which he sustained grievous injuries.
10.

In order to prove rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.KA-13-C-6770 by its driver,
the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1.
In the chief examination, PW.1 deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of car by its driver, the accident occurred.
On perusal of cross-examination of PW.1, nothing has been elicited from the mouth of PW.1 to disprove or disbelieve the case of petitioner.
In the cross examination, nothing to dispute or disbelieve the contention of petitioner related to accident and negligence of driver of offending vehicle could be elicited from the witness.

Nothing to dispute or rebut the contention of petitioner related to the Bhaskar Reddy.N vs Sunil K.S on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/140470210/
3 accident and cause of accident could be elicited during the cross examination.
11.

Further, in order to prove the accident and negligence of the driver of car, the petitioner produced Ex.P.2 First Information statement lodged by petitioner himself with the police on 01.08.2022 with respect to the accident occurred on 21.07.2022.
On the basis of first information lodged, the police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1 for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 337 of IPC and U/s. 134(a&b), 187 of M.V.Act.
In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle.
The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The petitioner also furnished sketch & spot mahazar which is marked as Ex.P.5 & 6.
The said document discloses that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said document.
In the mahazar also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.

The driver or owner of offending vehicle not placed satisfactory materials in order to show that the place of accident, as described in the mahazar and sketch, is against the actual facts at the place of accident.
Ex.P8 is the reply given by respondent No.1 to the notice issued by I.O under Sec.133 of IMV Act.
The said document discloses the involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The notice is given by the I.O alleging involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident and also alleging negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
Reply is given by respondent No.1 to the notice issued by I.O.
In the reply, there is no mention about non-involvement of offending vehicle in the accident and also about denial of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
Respondent No.1, being the owner of offending vehicle, could have denied the aspect of involvement of vehicle in the accident and denied negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
But, there are no recitals in the reply notice in that regard.
Ex.P.9 is the Wound certificate which discloses the aspect of injuries sustained by petitioner in the road traffic accident.
Ex.P.10 is the IMV Report, wherein the damages caused to the vehicles are mentioned.
The said document discloses the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.

The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the owner of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.279 & 338 of IPC and U/s.134(a&b), 187 of M.V.Act as per Ex.P.3.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.

In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondents and in the cross examination also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioners could be elicited.

No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioners pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.

4 12.
PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondents and in the cross examination, PW.1 stated that he was riding the motorcycle by the side of the car and the driver of the car suddenly opened the door.
PW.1 also stated that there was space towards the right side of the road in which the accident took place.
The said aspects do not indicate any negligence on the part of petitioner in the cause of accident.
As per the evidence of PW.1, the driver of the car stated to have suddenly opened the door that stated to have resulted in the accident.
The driver of the car has to look out for any vehicle passing by before opening the door of the car.
The opening of the door without observing movement of vehicle indicates negligence on the part of driver of the car.
The cross of PW.1 will not be of much assistance to the respondents in proving negligence on the part of petitioner in the cause of accident.
Mere presence of space on the right of the road will not sufficient to consider that the driver of the car need not be diligent while opening the door.
No satisfactory materials are being placed by the respondents in order to disprove the contention of petitioner related to accident and negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
13. Further, on perusal of the materials, there appears to be delay of twelve days in lodging first information statement.
The accident occurred on 21.07.2022.
As per Ex.P.2, first information statement, complainant himself has lodged a complaint with police on 01.08.2022.
As per the materials placed on record, there is twelve days delay in lodging complaint.
The complainant in his complaint explained that he was in hospital with the injured and thereafter lodged the complaint with the police.
Further, on perusal of hospital documents placed by the petitioner, immediately after the accident, the petitioner was taken to the hospital.
In general parlance, the injured as well as his family members think about providing best treatment to the patient rather than to lodge complaint before the police.
Only on the ground of delay in lodging complaint the claim cannot be doubted and the case cannot be dismissed.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Ravi Vs.
Badrinarayana in (2011) 4 SCC 693, held that delay in lodging a FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimants case.
In view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court, this tribunal cannot dismiss the petition only on the ground of delay in lodging the complaint.
No materials are placed to create doubt about contention of petitioner related to accident and negligence of respondent in the cause of accident.
Merely because there is delay in lodging the first information statement, the case of the petitioner cannot be considered to be doubtful.
14. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The respondents placed nothing before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
On perusal of entire record, it discloses that the rider of insured vehicle driven the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.10, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.KA-13- C-6770 by its driver and same has resulted in injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 held in the Affirmative.

Issue No.2:
In view of answering issue No.1 in the Affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc.
i) Towards injury, pain and suffering:- The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained injuries and underwent surgery and later discharged with an advice to take follow up treatment.
In order to prove the injuries sustained, the petitioner produced Wound certificate issued by Hosmat Hospital, Bengaluru, which is marked at Ex.P.9.
The said document discloses the aspects of injuries sustained by petitioner and that the injuries are grievous in nature.
So, on perusal of records, the petitioner appears to have taken treatment at the hospital as an inpatient.
The petitioner produced Ex.P11 & 12 - Discharge Summaries, issued by Hosmat Hospital, Bengaluru and examined Dr.Krishan Prasad as PW.2 and got marked documents at Ex.P19 to 21.

PW.2/doctor deposed that he examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and stated that the petitioner is having permanent physical disability of upper and lower limb at 51% and to the whole body at 17%.
By considering the injuries and facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that the compensation of .50,000/- appears just and reasonable towards pain and suffering.
(ii) Towards Medical Expenses:
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards medical expenses.
The petitioner contended that he took treatment at the Hospital.
The petitioner produced 39 medical bills amounting to .3,02,793/- which are marked at Ex.P.14 and 12 medical prescriptions which are marked at Ex.P.13.
The respondent not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or disprove the said document.

PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondent and in the cross examination also,
nothing to rebut or doubt the medical bills, is elicited.
The respondents not rebutted the medical bills by placing cogent evidence.

So, this tribunal is of the view that compensation of .3,02,793/-
appears just and reasonable towards medical expenses.
(iii) Towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant charges:
On perusal of records, the accident occurred on 21.07.2022 and the petitioner took treatment as an inpatient at the hospital.
On perusal of evidence, the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient at the Hospital as he sustained injuries.
During the time of treatment, the petitioner might have required good food and extra nourishment.

The petitioner produced Ex.P.11 & 12 - Discharge Summaries issued by Hosmat Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein it is mentioned that petitioner took treatment as an inpatient from 21.07.2022 to 23.07.2022 and again from 31.08.2022 to 03.09.2022 i.e., for a period of 07 days.

Considering the said facts, the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of .500/- per day for 07 days to a sum of .3,500/- appears just and reasonable towards food, extra nourishment and medical attendant.

(iv) Towards Conveyance:

(v) Towards loss of income during treatment:
The petitioner contended that he was an Agriculturist cum milk vendor and earning a sum of .25,000/- per month.
In order to prove the income, the petitioner not produced any satisfactory documents.
The petitioner not furnished any satisfactory materials to show that he was earning .25,000/- per month, as contended by him.
No materials are placed by petitioner in order to substantiate her contention pertaining to his occupation and income.
In the absence of satisfactory materials, the notional income of petitioner is to be taken into consideration.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the notional income of the petitioner considered as .15,500/-.
On perusal of record, it appears that petitioner might not have attended his work for some time due to accidental injuries.
Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for .20,000/- towards loss of income during treatment.
(vi) Towards Loss of future earning capacity:
The petitioner has contended that due to accident, he was admitted as an inpatient at hospital and sustained permanent disablement.
The materials on record disclose the aspect of petitioner sustaining injuries to left index finger and left leg.

The petitioner examined Dr.Krishan Prasad, working as Orthopaedic Surgeon at Hosmat Hospital,
Bengaluru as PW.2.
PW.2/Doctor examined the patient clinically and radiologically to assess disabilities.
The doctor deposed that petitioner sustained fracture to left index finger proximal phalanx and fracture of left leg hematoma.
PW.2 further deposed that k-wiring done to left index finger and incision to left leg hematoma and drainage was done.
PW.2 further deposed that relating to skin necrosis of left leg,
wound debridement of left leg was done and split skin grafting was done to left leg and later discharged

. Further, PW.2 stated that on recent examination, for the purpose of assessment of disability, it was noticed that petitioner has left index finger proximal phalanx fracture gone for malunion and deformity.
The petitioner is stated to have pain and stiffness in the left hand and has difficulty in making a fist.
The left leg is stated to have been swollen with stiffness of the knee with a healed skin graft and skin graft areas are numb and itch a lot.

Further, on recent examination for the purpose of assessment of disability, it was noticed that he has pain and great difficulty in kneeling, squatting, sitting cross legged and climbing stairs and slopes and he needs frequent periods of rest to relieve his pain and swelling in his left leg and his left knee is painful.
PW.2 further deposed that the petitioner states that his left hand and index are painful and stiff and unable to make a fist and difficulty in Bhaskar Reddy.

The doctor examined the petitioner for assessment of disability and assessed the disability of both upper and lower limbs at 51% and to the whole body at 17%.
In order to prove the disability, doctor has produced Ex.P.19 to 21 i.e., OP records, IP records and X-rays.
PW.2 stated in the evidence that the fractures are united and skin grafting done to petitioner is healed.
PW.2 not stated that the petitioner could not be able to do his routine activities in a normal way.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the petitioner to show that the petitioner is unable to do any work at all.
The injuries sustained by petitioner do not appear to cause much problem in doing his activities.
By considering the oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the petitioner can do his work with difficulty.
As per ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another and considering facts and circumstances of the case, the functional disability is assessed at 10%.

sentences.text: In order to prove age, the petitioner produced Ex.P.17 - Notarized Copy of Aadhaar Card, wherein his date of birth is mentioned as 10.10.1956.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to controvert or rebut the documents furnished by petitioner related to the age.
As per the documents furnished by petitioner, his age appears to be 66 years at the time of accident.
Accident occurred on 21.07.2022.
In the absence of materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the age.
As per the materials on record, the age of petitioner is 66 years at the time of accident and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier.
As per Smt.Sarla Verma case multiplier applicable is '05'.
As per ratio laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay Kumar and another, this tribunal not deducted personal expenses of petitioner out of his gross income.

17. In MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Page No.7 at Para No.15 held as follows:
"However, the provisions of Section 149(1) of the Act to the extent they speak of interest payable on the compensation amount is in the nature of an exception to the general law enacted in 169 of the M.V.Act and therefore, the provisions of Section 34 of CPC to that extent become invocable on the general principles of construction of statutes namely the special law overrides the general law.

Thus, in the given circumstances of this case,
interest at the rate of more than 6% could not have been awarded."

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above judgment, the petitioner is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .5,09,293/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Nine Thousand Two Hundred and Ninety Three only) with interest at 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and  severally liable to pay compensation to  petitioner.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.

In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 40% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank and the remaining 60% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification.

After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.

The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.

In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of car by its driver.
The respondents, being the R.C. owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 21.07.2022 at about 07.00 p.m., at Pipeline Road, Yeshwanthapura,
Opposite Trumpti Wine Store, Bengaluru, when he was riding a Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-HY- 0999, due to the rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.KA-13-C- 6770 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition? If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3. What order or award?
Findings of this tribunal on the above issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative;
 Issue No.3 : As per final order for  the following:-
 -:REASONS:-
9. Issue No.1:- The petitioner contended that on 21.07.2022 at about 07.00 p.m., accident occurred at Pipeline Road, Yeshwanthapura, Opposite Trumpti Wine Store, Bengaluru, when he was riding Motor Cycle bearing Regn.No.KA-04-HY-0999, due to the rash and negligent driving of Car bearing Regn.No.KA-13- C-6770 by its driver in which he sustained grievous injuries.
10.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.
In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials in order to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioners pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
As per the evidence of PW.1, the driver of the car stated to have suddenly opened the door that stated to have resulted in the accident.
The driver of the car has to look out for any vehicle passing by before opening the door of the car.
The opening of the door without observing movement of vehicle indicates negligence on the part of driver of the car.
The cross of PW.1 will not be of much assistance to the respondents in proving negligence on the part of petitioner in the cause of accident.
Mere presence of space on the right of the road will not sufficient to consider that the driver of the car need not be diligent while opening the door.
No satisfactory materials are being placed by the respondents in order to disprove the contention of petitioner related to accident and negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
Further, on perusal of hospital documents placed by the petitioner, immediately after the accident, the petitioner was taken to the hospital.
In general parlance, the injured as well as his family members think about providing best treatment to the patient rather than to lodge complaint before the police.
Only on the ground of delay in lodging complaint the claim cannot be doubted and the case cannot be dismissed.
Merely because there is delay in lodging the first information statement, the case of the petitioner cannot be considered to be doubtful.
14. The respondents not placed satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The respondents placed nothing before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
On perusal of entire record, it discloses that the rider of insured vehicle driven the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the petitioner to show that the petitioner is unable to do any work at all.
The injuries sustained by petitioner do not appear to cause much problem in doing his activities.
By considering the oral and documentary evidence and facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the petitioner can do his work with difficulty.
As per ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Raj Kumar V/s. Ajay kumar and another and considering facts and circumstances of the case, the functional disability is assessed at 10%.
In the absence of materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the age.
As per the materials on record, the age of petitioner is 66 years at the time of accident and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case, the tribunal is of the view that compensation of .10,000/- appears just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future amenities.
opennyai_summary.decision:
The petitioner is entitled for .93,000/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case .20,000/- is just and reasonable under the head deprivation of future medical expenses.
16. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:

Total compensation .5,09,293/-
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation of .5,09,293/-.
In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above judgment, the petitioner is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
So,
the respondents being the R.C. owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
19. Issue No.3:
In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .5,09,293/- (Rupees Five Lakhs Nine Thousand Two Hundred and Ninety Three only) with interest at 6% p.a.,
from the date of petition till realization.
Respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and  severally liable to pay compensation to  petitioner.
Respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 40% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank and the remaining 60% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification.
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA.No.2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated 19.8.2019.
The petitioner hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contained compulsorily photographs of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhaar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount with interest thereon by respondent, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission from the Tribunal.
Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner on proper verification and identification or credit said amount to her account after expiry of three years period of deposit,
without waiting for further order of court.
The Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
